items.definition: a product or company name that customers recognize and connect with certain qualities
exampleSentences: The company spent years building a brand that customers trust.
This shampoo is a popular brand among young shoppers.
They redesigned the logo to give the brand a fresher look.

items.definition: a series of planned actions to achieve a particular goal, such as selling a product
exampleSentences: The marketing team launched a new campaign to promote the app.
Their ad campaign ran on social media for six weeks.
She is planning the campaign's next phase.

items.definition: the specific group of people that a company wants to reach with its product or message
exampleSentences: Teenagers are the target audience for this new sneaker line.
The ad's tone matches the target audience perfectly.
Before designing the campaign, the team studied their target audience closely.

items.definition: the percentage of total sales in a market that one company controls
exampleSentences: The company gained market share after the price cut.
Rivals are competing fiercely for market share in this region.
Losing market share worried the executives.

items.definition: a company or person that competes with another in the same business or market
exampleSentences: The two competitors offer almost identical prices.
She studies competitors before setting a new price.
A new competitor entered the market last spring.

items.definition: to introduce a new product or service to the public, or the event of doing this
exampleSentences: The company will launch its new phone next month.
The product launch attracted a lot of media attention.
They launched the app in three countries at once.

items.definition: to tell the public about a product or service in order to sell it
exampleSentences: Small businesses often advertise on local radio.
The store is advertising a big sale this weekend.
They advertised the new flavor on billboards across the city.

items.definition: to help sell a product by advertising it or making people notice it
exampleSentences: Influencers were paid to promote the new drink.
The store promotes seasonal items near the entrance.
They promoted the sale through social media posts.

items.definition: a small design or symbol that a company puts on its products and advertisements so people can recognize it
exampleSentences: The company's logo appears on every box it ships.
They hired a designer to create a simpler logo for the brand.
Customers recognized the logo even without the company name.

items.definition: the quality of continuing to support a particular brand or company
exampleSentences: The card rewards customer loyalty with points.
Good service builds loyalty over time.
The brand has earned strong loyalty among its fans.

items.definition: comments from customers about how well a product or service works
exampleSentences: The company collects feedback after every purchase.
Customer feedback helped improve the app.
She left positive feedback about the new packaging.

items.definition: a set of questions used to find out what people think or want
exampleSentences: The team sent a survey to recent buyers.
Results from the survey shaped the new design.
Customers filled out a short survey after checkout.

items.definition: a group of people sharing features such as age, income, or location that marketers study
exampleSentences: The brand targets a younger demographic this year.
Each demographic responds differently to the ad.
The survey broke results down by demographic.

items.definition: the materials and design used to wrap or contain a product for sale
exampleSentences: The new packaging uses less plastic than before.
Bright packaging helps the product stand out on shelves.
Customers complained that the packaging was hard to open.

items.definition: a person with many online followers whose opinions affect what those followers buy, and who is often paid to promote products
exampleSentences: The brand hired an influencer to review its skincare line.
Influencers posted unboxing videos of the new phone.
Small brands often work with local influencers.

items.definition: a business that sells products directly to customers, often in a store
exampleSentences: The retailer stocks the brand in over two hundred stores.
Online retailers now outsell many traditional stores.
The retailer offered an exclusive discount on launch day.

items.definition: a person who buys and uses products or services
exampleSentences: Consumers are becoming more interested in sustainable products.
The survey measured consumer confidence this year.
Rising prices changed consumer behavior.

items.definition: a small, specific part of a market that appeals to a particular group
exampleSentences: The company found a profitable niche selling vegan snacks.
They focus on a niche market instead of competing with big brands.
Her store serves a niche of collectors and hobbyists.

items.definition: a short, memorable phrase used to advertise a product or brand
exampleSentences: The company's slogan appears on every advertisement.
They tested five different slogans before choosing one.
A catchy slogan can stay in customers' minds for years.

items.definition: to pay some of the costs of an event or team in exchange for advertising; also a company that does this
exampleSentences: The soft drink brand sponsors the city marathon every year.
Local shops sponsored the town's youth basketball team.
The festival's main sponsor placed banners around the stage.

items.definition: the process of getting products from a company to the stores or customers that buy them
exampleSentences: The company improved its distribution across rural areas.
Poor distribution meant the product was hard to find.
They signed a deal to expand distribution overseas.

items.definition: a store or shop where a company's products are sold
exampleSentences: The brand opened its first outlet in the capital.
Discounted items are sold at the factory outlet.
Each outlet follows the same store design.

items.definition: a feature that makes a product different from and better than similar products sold by competitors
exampleSentences: The phone's unique selling point is a battery that lasts a week.
Every advertisement should make the product's unique selling point clear.
Fast delivery became the company's main unique selling point.

items.definition: to change a company's name, logo, or image to create a new identity
exampleSentences: The airline rebranded after years of poor reviews.
They rebranded the drink with brighter colors and a new name.
A rebrand can attract customers who ignored the old image.

items.definition: a printed or digital voucher that gives a customer a discount
exampleSentences: She used a coupon to get free shipping.
The store emailed coupons to loyal customers.
Coupons drove a lot of traffic to the website last week.

items.definition: a recommendation that leads a new customer to a business
exampleSentences: Many new clients come through customer referrals.
The company rewards referrals with a small discount.
Word spread through referrals rather than advertising.

items.definition: a statement from a satisfied customer used to promote a product
exampleSentences: The website displays testimonials from happy customers.
A strong testimonial can convince new buyers to trust the brand.
They asked users for testimonials after the trial period.

items.definition: the passing of information about a product between people, without advertising
exampleSentences: The restaurant grew popular through word of mouth alone.
Good word of mouth is more powerful than any ad.
News about the sale spread by word of mouth.

items.definition: the group of people who regularly buy from a particular company
exampleSentences: The company built a loyal customer base over ten years.
A wider customer base means steadier sales.
The app lost part of its customer base after the redesign.

items.definition: the process of gathering information about customers and competitors before selling a product
exampleSentences: The team carried out market research before the launch.
Market research showed strong demand for the flavor.
They rely on market research to guide new designs.

items.definition: how to use the passive voice to describe processes, results and reports without naming who did the action
items.explanationTR:
In business reports, writers often use the passive voice to focus on an action or result rather than on who performed it. This is common when the person responsible is unknown, unimportant, or already clear from the situation.

Form the passive with a form of "be" plus the past participle:
• Present simple passive: The product is tested before release.
• Past simple passive: The campaign was launched in March.
• Present perfect passive: The results have been reviewed by the team.
• Future simple passive: The new packaging will be introduced next season.
• Past perfect passive: The survey had been completed before the launch date.

Add "by + agent" only when the agent matters:
• The rebranding was designed by an outside agency.

In marketing and business writing, the passive keeps attention on products, customers, and results rather than on the writer's own team:
• Customer feedback is collected after every purchase.
• Over a thousand coupons were redeemed last month.

Don't overuse the passive, though. When the person or thing performing the action is the point of the sentence, the active voice is clearer and more natural.

questions.explanationTR: Routine, repeated actions with an unstated subject take the present simple passive (is collected); "collects" and "has collected" are active forms that would need a stated subject performing the action.

questions.prompt: The new marketing campaign ---- last month.
questions.explanationTR: The finished time marker "last month" needs the past simple, and the campaign receives the action, so the passive "was launched" is correct; "has been launched" is present perfect, which cannot be used with a finished time like "last month."

questions.prompt: Over one thousand coupons ---- since the sale began.
questions.explanationTR: "Since the sale began" signals an action continuing up to now, so the present perfect passive "have been redeemed" is needed, agreeing with the plural subject "coupons"; the future perfect "will have been redeemed" describes a later deadline, not the present result.

questions.prompt: The rebranding ---- by an outside design agency.
questions.explanationTR: Because the agent ("an outside design agency") is stated and important, the passive "was designed" is used with "by"; "is designing" would wrongly make the rebranding itself the one doing the designing.

questions.prompt: Starting next year, the product ---- to every retailer in the region.
questions.explanationTR: "Starting next year" points to the future, and the product receives the action, so the future passive "will be distributed" is correct; "will distribute" is active and would mean the product itself does the distributing, and "would have been distributed" is a conditional form that does not fit a real future plan.

questions.prompt: The market research ---- before the launch date was even set.
questions.explanationTR: The research finished before another past event ("the launch date was even set"), so the past perfect passive "had been completed" is needed; the present perfect "has been completed" would place the action too close to now.

questions.prompt: The survey results ---- in the company newsletter last week.
questions.explanationTR: "Results" is plural, so it needs the plural passive "were published"; "was published" wrongly treats "results" as singular, and "had been publishing" is an unnecessary, unnatural aspect here.

questions.prompt: An outside agency ---- the new slogan for last year's campaign.
questions.explanationTR: Here "an outside agency" is the subject performing the action, so the active "created" is correct; using a passive form would incorrectly turn the agency into the receiver of the action.

items.definition: A short article about a drink's marketing campaign, with eight gaps to complete

questions.prompt: Before choosing a name for the new drink, the company invested heavily in ---- to learn about customer preferences.
questions.explanationTR: Market research is the process of gathering information about customers before selling a product, which fits a company preparing to choose a name; customer feedback comes only after a purchase, so it does not fit "before choosing a name."

questions.prompt: The design team then focused on ---- that would stand out on crowded store shelves.
questions.explanationTR: Packaging is the material and design that wraps a product, which is what a design team works on so that it stands out on shelves; distribution is the process of getting products to stores, not something that is seen on a shelf.

questions.prompt: Marketers chose teenagers and young adults as the ---- for the campaign.
questions.explanationTR: The target audience is the specific group a campaign is aimed at, which fits choosing teenagers and young adults; market share refers to a company's percentage of total sales, not a group of people.

questions.prompt: To reach that group quickly, the brand hired a well-known ---- to post about the drink online.
questions.explanationTR: An influencer is a person with online followers who is paid to promote products, matching someone hired to post online; a sponsor typically funds an event rather than posting personal content.

questions.prompt: The company opened its first flagship ---- in the capital, complete with tasting stations.
questions.explanationTR: An outlet is a single store location, which fits a "flagship" opening in one city; a retailer refers more generally to a selling business, not one specific store.

questions.prompt: Within a month, most major ---- were stocking the drink in their stores nationwide.
questions.explanationTR: Retailers are businesses that sell products to customers in stores, so they are the ones who stock the drink; competitors make or sell rival products and would not stock it, and the other options are not businesses at all.

questions.prompt: Even without more advertising, satisfied customers kept telling their friends about the drink, proof of the power of ----.
questions.explanationTR: Word of mouth describes information passed between people without advertising, matching customers telling their friends; a testimonial is a formal written or spoken statement, not casual conversation.

questions.prompt: A year later, the brand introduced a rewards card to build customer ---- and encourage repeat purchases.
questions.explanationTR: Customer loyalty is the ongoing support of a brand, which fits a rewards card aimed at repeat purchases; feedback is comments about a product, not the ongoing relationship a loyalty card targets.
